Commentary.Commentary: Back for the chase. The players are out in the middle. Ben Duckett and Jamie Smith to open for England. Jayden Seales to bowl with he new ball.
...THE CHASE...

England won't be much disappointed as well. They might feel they have given 10-20 runs extra or could have cleared the tails with a better plan but still, this is a chaseable total. England bowled well throughout the innings. Adil Rashid was the pick of the bowlers as he picked 3 wickets. Even their fielding was fantastic today as compared to the second ODI. They have a decent job and will back themselves to chase it down however, they have to be careful of the overcast conditions and the new ball which could be lethal. Stay tuned for the chase.

A fighting total from West Indies and they'll be proud of themselves for the effort they have shown. They'll be happy with how their tail enders have performed with the bat. West Indies were 154/7 when they lost a well set Sherfane Rutherford and it felt that the visitors will struggle to even reach 200 but Gudakesh Motie and Alzarri Joseph joined hands to add 91 runs to the board. Motie played the anchoring role while Alzarri Joseph put a lot of pressure on the opposition with his quick fire 41. Before the mid rain-break, West Indies were in a lot of trouble but will be happy with how things have panned out.
OUT! BOWLED! A wicket of the final delivery! A good length delivery on leg, Motie makes room and tries to pull it low but misses and it crashes the leg pole. West Indies finish with 251/9.

UPDATE - 11.47 am GMT - The West Indies players have arrived at the Kennington Oval. We have an official toss update as well. The toss will happen at 12.10 pm GMT and the action will start at 12.30 pm GMT.

Update - Well, surprisingly, the West Indies team are reportedly stuck in heavy traffic and as a result the toss has been delayed. Strange and unusual to see this happening on an international level. Stay tuned.

Despite losing both the English openers on a duck, the hosts confidently chased down the total with Joe Root grabbing the headlines. He became England's record ODI run-scorer in the process and his unbeaten 166 helped England clinch the series. West Indies have nothing but to play for pride while England will hope to sweep the series. With the series in their pocket, expect a couple of changes from the home side. Stay tuned for the toss and other updates.

The second ODI was a more evenly fought contest than the first game. The top order of the Winides contributed heavily to their overall total with Keacy Carty leading the chart with a magnificent 100 against a quality English line up. However, the calculative approach by the Windies backfired as the visitors tried to up the ante in the slog overs but instead lost heaps of wickets and eventually bailed out with a score less than what was expected.

Hello everyone to the third and final ODI between England and West Indies. The hosts have taken an unassailable lead of 2-0 and will be raring to start the summer tour with a clean sweep in front of the home fans, while West Indies will hope to get a result in their favour and avoid a heart-wrenching series sweep.
...MATCH DAY...

We are here at the iconic Kennington Oval in London, where West Indies will take on England in the third and final ODI of the series. With England having an unassailable lead of 2-0 in the series,  West Indies will be fighting for pride and a crucial victory to avoid a clean sweep, while England will be looking to assert their dominance on home soil. The second ODI in Cardiff was much closer, but Joe Root's superb unbeaten innings of 166, which also made him England's record ODI run-scorer, led the hosts to a thrilling three-wicket victory while chasing 309. After getting a major setback in the first ODI, West Indies bounced back stronger in the second ODI with a brilliant batting performance with a scintillating century from Keacy Carty and well-supported half-centuries from skipper Shai Hope and Brandon King. In the bowling department, Alzarri Joseph has been a standout, claiming four wickets in the second ODI. The West Indies will be hoping to capitalize on their better batting performance from the second ODI in order to salvage some pride and showcase their potential. On a usually strong batting surface at The Oval, the West Indies will need a collective effort, especially in their middle order, to put pressure on the English bowlers and build a competitive score or chase successfully. Talking about England, under new white-ball captain Harry Brook, England hasn't put a foot wrong in the first two ODIs. While chasing a mammoth target of 309, the home side got off to a shaky start as they lost their two wickets for just two runs. However, a match-winning knock of 166* from the experienced campaigner Joe Root and important contributions from Skipper Harry Brook and Will Jacks helped them to cross the finishing line with 3 wickets and 7 balls to spare. On the bowling front, England's bowlers had a mixed performance, with Adil Rashid and Saqib Mahmood picking up 4 and 3 wickets, respectively. England will be keen to maintain their momentum and finish the series on a high. Given England's current form and the fact that they have sealed the series, they may be tempted to experiment with their playing XI, but maintaining winning momentum will be a top goal. The West Indies, on the other hand, have everything to play for and will be eager to secure a victory before the T20I series. Expect a good game of cricket with both sides eager to make their mark. The Oval crowd will be expecting an exciting end to the ODI series.
